transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. I, um... I guess I'm just here because I've been feeling a little tired lately? Well, maybe more than a little. I just feel kind of worn out all the time, even if I've been in bed for a full night. It's silly, I know everyone gets tired, but it feels like my body is made of sandbags. Just getting through my workday at the marketing firm, or even doing something small like folding laundry, it just takes everything I have right now. I hope that makes sense? I'm sure it's probably nothing major, but I just wanted to get it checked out, if that's okay.
Have you noticed any changes in how you feel about activities you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I usually try to be really active and involved. I used to always make time for hiking, and going to yoga, and working in my garden. Oh, and taking bird photos—I really love doing that. 

But lately... I don't know, I feel terrible about it, but I just keep canceling on my friends. And my camera has just been sitting in the closet for weeks. It's not that I don't want to be a fun, active person anymore, it just... honestly, right now, none of it really feels worth the effort? 

I'm sure it's just because I've been so tired from work, right? I hope it's okay that I'm just taking a little break from all those things... does that sound normal to you?
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Well... I mean, I don't want to sound ungrateful for my life or anything, because I really do have a lot of good things going on. But, um... yeah, I guess I have been feeling a bit down. 

It's just this... this heavy, flat feeling right in my chest. Most days I wake up with it, and it just kind of stays there. Sometimes I'll just sit at the kitchen table with my coffee, staring out at the yard, and... I don't know, it's embarrassing to say, but I just feel like there's no good version of the future coming? Like everything is just kind of gray. 

I know I shouldn't think that way, and I try really hard to snap out of it. It's probably just a phase, right? I mean, everyone has days where they feel a little gloomy for no reason... is that something you hear a lot?
Has it felt like you don’t get any pleasure or satisfaction out of things you used to enjoy, like hiking, yoga, or taking photos?

Um, yeah, I guess that's... that's exactly it. It's like I mentioned before, with the hiking and the yoga and the photos. I really do want to be the kind of person who enjoys those things, I promise I do. It's just... 

When I look at my camera, or think about going out to the garden, I just feel so... empty about it? There's no spark anymore. It just feels like another chore on the to-do list, and I'm already so tired. I know I shouldn't be letting it all go, and I feel awful about canceling on my friends so much. 

I'm trying not to be lazy about it, I really am. It's just hard to force yourself to do things when there's no... no joy at the end of it, you know? Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too negative.
Have you noticed a significant loss of energy or feel that everything takes extra effort, even when you're not physically tired?

Well, um... yes. Actually, that's kind of a big part of why I finally decided to come in. I hate to admit it, because I really try to just push through and be productive, but... I just feel worn out all the time lately. 

It's like, even after I spend a full night in bed, I wake up and my body just feels like it's made of sandbags. I try so hard to keep up with everything, but just getting through a normal workday, or even doing something small like folding the laundry... it just takes absolutely everything I have right now. 

I feel terrible that I can't just handle my normal responsibilities without feeling this way. Is that... does that sound like something you see a lot? I really hope I don't just sound like I'm making excuses for being tired...
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I know sometimes people stop eating when they feel down, but I've always been pretty good about making sure I have my meals. I don't want to cause any other health problems, you know? 

I think my weight has stayed pretty much the same. I try to make healthy choices when I can, even when I'm feeling so tired. I haven't really noticed my clothes fitting differently or anything like that. 

I hope that's okay? Like, is it normal to feel this way but still be eating normally? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information...
Have you noticed that your thoughts have been slower than usual, or that it's harder to make decisions, even about small things?

Um, well... I guess I have noticed a little bit of that. I really try not to let it affect my work, I promise. I'm usually very sharp, but lately... 

It's just, sometimes at work, I'll be looking at some survey results or reading a client email, and I'll read it like three times and realize I haven't actually absorbed a single word. And making choices, even silly little ones... like, just deciding which spreadsheet I should open first to start my day can feel just... weirdly impossible? 

I feel so bad about it, because I know my team relies on me to be on top of things. I'm trying really hard to stay focused and not let anything slip through the cracks. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound like I'm just being incompetent at my job... is it normal for things to feel a bit foggy like that?
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough, or been blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?

Well, um... I guess I have been struggling a little bit with that. I try really hard not to be too hard on myself, because I know it doesn't help anything, but... 

Lately, I just keep replaying this decision we made about our mortgage. I keep telling myself I was just... so selfish and reckless. I feel like I put our whole household at risk. I mean, my husband is so sweet, he keeps reminding me that we made the decision together and that it's fine, but... I just can't shake this feeling that I messed everything up. 

I feel awful even complaining about it, because I know I have a good life and a supportive husband. I shouldn't be dwelling on things like this, right? I just... I hope I don't sound ungrateful or like I'm just throwing a pity party. Is it common to get stuck on feeling like you've ruined things, even when people tell you you haven't?
Have you found yourself thinking about death or feeling like life isn't worth living lately?

Oh... um... well... I know I shouldn't think this way, and I really don't want to upset you or make you think I'm, you know, a danger to myself or anything. I try to stay positive, I really do.

But... sometimes, especially late at night when it's quiet... I catch myself thinking that maybe my husband might just be better off without me. Like, without all this burden I'm causing with the mortgage and everything. 

I haven't made a plan or done anything like that, I promise! I would never want to actually do something to hurt him. It's just... the thought keeps coming back, and it honestly scares me a little bit. I know it's a terrible thing to think, and I feel so guilty for even letting it cross my mind. 

I hope you don't think less of me for admitting that. Is it... is it normal for people to have thoughts like that when they're feeling this overwhelmed? I just want to be honest so you can help me fix it...
Have you had any previous episodes where you felt this way for a period of time, or is this the first time you've experienced these symptoms?

Um... I'm trying to think. I really want to give you the right answer, but... I don't think so? 

I mean, I've definitely had periods where I was stressed with work projects or feeling a little run down, because everyone gets like that sometimes, right? I always just try to push through and keep a smile on so I don't bother anyone. But feeling this... this stuck, and having those awful thoughts... I'm pretty sure this is the first time it's been this bad. 

I hope it's okay that I'm not a hundred percent sure... I feel a little silly not knowing my own history better, and I don't want to give you bad information. But no, I really don't recall ever feeling quite like this in the past. Is it normal for it to just sort of hit you out of the blue like this?
Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt down, lost interest in things, or experienced similar symptoms that lasted for at least two weeks or more?

Oh... I see what you're asking. Um, as far as the past goes, before this, I really don't think I've ever had a time that lasted that long. But... if you mean right now? I probably should have mentioned this sooner, I'm sorry. I just... I feel a little embarrassed that I haven't been able to just pull myself together. 

But this current feeling... the depressed, slowed-down, exhausted part... it's actually been going on most days for about the past two months. I kept hoping I could just shake it off and get back to normal so I wouldn't have to bother anyone with it, but it's just stuck around. I hope it's okay that I waited this long to come in and get help... Does that give you what you need to know?
Have you ever had a time in your life before this one where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had similar symptoms that lasted for at least two weeks?

Oh, I'm so sorry, I probably didn't explain myself very clearly just a second ago. I know I can be a little scattered right now, and I really don't mean to make your job harder. 

But um... no, before this current stretch we just talked about, I really haven't ever had a period like that. Not for two whole weeks, anyway. I've always been able to just sort of... push through any normal stress and keep things moving at work, you know? Just put on a brave face so I don't let anyone down or drop the ball on my research reports. 

So, looking back... no, nothing like this in the past. I really hope I'm being helpful... I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to figure this out. Did I answer that right?

Have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually high-spirited, extremely energetic, or unusually irritable — maybe even to the point where others noticed a change in your behavior or it caused problems in your life?

Um... well... I don't know if I'd say "unusually" high-spirited, because I really try to stay positive and energetic for my team, you know? I want to be a good influence. But... I guess there was a time recently where it maybe got a little intense? I hope that doesn't make me sound difficult to work with...

It was right after my husband and I signed the mortgage papers on our new house. For the first few weeks, I just felt... I don't know, almost lit up? Like I was just unstoppable and could tackle everything at work and at home without even trying. But then... and I feel terrible admitting this... I would suddenly get so frustrated. Like, if a coworker was a little slow getting me a research file, or if my husband didn't do something exactly right, I would just snap at them. It was like one minute I was on top of the world, and the next I was just so short-tempered over tiny delays. 

I always apologized right away, of course. I hate being that kind of person... I really don't want you to think I'm normally like that. I just... I had so much energy, it almost felt like it was spilling over into impatience. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you're asking about?
How long did that period of feeling unusually energetic and irritable last — was it just a few days, or longer than that?

Oh, gosh... um, I'm really sorry, I don't actually know for sure. I feel terrible that I don't have a precise answer for you. In my line of work, I'm usually so good with tracking data and details, so it's a little embarrassing that I can't give you a clear timeline for myself. 

I just... I didn't really write it down or keep track of the days, you know? It could have been a few days, or maybe a little longer, but it's all just kind of a blur of unpacking boxes and trying to keep up at the office so I wouldn't fall behind. I really hope it's okay that I don't know the exact duration... I'm trying my best to remember, I just don't want to give you the wrong information. Is it alright if I'm not totally sure?

So, just to be clear, have you ever had a period of time — even just a few days — where you felt unusually energetic, unusually irritable, or high-spirited to the point that others noticed a change in your behavior or it caused some problems in your life?

Oh, yes! I'm so sorry, I probably rambled a bit too much earlier and didn't give you a clear enough answer. I really don't mean to make you repeat yourself. 

But yes, to be completely clear, that is what happened. Like I was saying, in the first few weeks after we signed the mortgage papers, I really did feel almost lit up and completely unstoppable one minute... and then the next, I was snapping at my husband or my coworkers over tiny little delays. I felt awful about it because I really pride myself on being easy to work with. But yes, I did have that kind of energy and irritability. 

I hope I'm making more sense now. Did I answer it right this time?

Have you ever had a period of time — even just a few days — where you felt so energetic, high-spirited, or irritable that it was a noticeable change from your usual self, even if others didn’t say anything about it?

Um, yes... I'm really sorry if I'm making this difficult, I feel like you're having to ask me the same thing again and I must not be explaining it well at all. I really want to be helpful. 

But yes, exactly that. It was a very noticeable change from my usual self, even if people were too polite to say anything to me directly. Like I mentioned, right after we got the house, I had that period where I just felt so incredibly energized and capable, like I could do absolutely anything... but then it would turn into that awful irritability where I was snapping at my husband or getting short with my team over the smallest things. 

I'm usually very even-tempered, I promise. I try so hard to be a positive presence. So yes, that was definitely a time where I was acting very differently than I normally do. Does that help? I really hope I'm giving you the right information this time.
